causeAnalysis.verdict: CONFIRMED BY CONFIG, not just correlation
causeAnalysis.mechanism: The e2e-tests job Build step runs pnpm run build --filter=!ai-gateway, a full turbo build, on a 4vCPU blacksmith runner. worker depends on @langfuse/native, and @langfuse/native is also selected directly by that filter. turbo.json pins @langfuse/native#build to cache:false with outputs:[], so turbo can never replay it: a cargo --release build runs on every single e2e run. The e2e job has no Rust toolchain setup step, so rustup is triggered implicitly inside Build.
causeAnalysis.authorsRationale: The turbo.json comment reads: napi build compiles a host-specific binary and Cargo already caches incrementally in target/, so never replay this task from the turbo cache. That premise holds on a developer laptop where target/ persists. On an ephemeral CI runner target/ does not persist and no cargo cache action exists, so the reasoning does not carry over to CI.

suggestedDiff.theme: Stop building the Rust addon in the e2e job
suggestedDiff.verification: Static derivation of the turbo build closure from pnpm-workspace.yaml + each package.json + turbo.json, run in-sandbox. pnpm and turbo are not installed in this sandbox, so turbo run build --dry=json could not be invoked; the closure was reproduced from config instead.
suggestedDiff.verificationResult: CURRENT --filter=!ai-gateway selects 7 build tasks including @langfuse/native#build and worker#build. PROPOSED --filter=!ai-gateway --filter=!worker --filter=!@langfuse/native selects 5, dropping both, and still retains web#build, @langfuse/ee#build, @langfuse/shared#build, @repo/eslint-plugin#build and @repo/in-app-agent-sandbox-runtime#build.
suggestedDiff.caughtDuringVerification: Excluding only worker is NOT sufficient. @langfuse/native is itself a selected workspace package with a build script, so it survives a worker-only exclusion. Both filters are required.
suggestedDiff.safety: web/playwright.config.ts starts webServer with npm run start in web only. The e2e suite never loads the worker or the native addon.

followUps: Verify next week whether the suggested e2e filter change (if applied) returns e2e Build to ~42-48s and perceived to ~190s. That is the falsifiable prediction.

If the filter change is rejected, the alternative lever is making @langfuse/native#build cacheable in turbo.json with declared outputs. Do not propose it casually: the cache:false was deliberate and caching a host-specific binary across differing runner images is genuinely risky. It would help every job that builds the worker, not just e2e.
